# The backbone {.unnumbered}

A PhD student explains the whole thesis to a bachelor student. Wins, ties and losses for DRL are all part of the story.

The thesis is not "DRL wins". It is how we found out what a win really rested on.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  Q["THE QUESTION<br/>When does a learning controller beat tuned rules<br/>on a freeway, and how do we check that honestly?"]
  B["TEST BENCH<br/>r2m3 in SUMO<br/>3 lanes, 2 on-ramps"]
  C["CONTESTANTS<br/>no control, tuned rules,<br/>v3w per-CAV PPO"]
  R["REFEREE<br/>protocol fixed before data,<br/>fresh seeds, paired stats"]
  A["REAL-WORLD ANCHOR<br/>NGSIM / MnDOT data"]
  E["THE E30 STORY<br/>edge found, confirmed, replicated at 300 m,<br/>WORSE at 600 m"]
  M["CAUSE<br/>SUMO mergers stop at a short lane end;<br/>the learner stands less there (limit M1)"]
  T["THE CLAIM<br/>scoped to this plant and 295-m lanes;<br/>method lesson; null DRL allowed"]
  Q --> B & C & R & A
  B & C & R & A --> E --> M --> T
```

| # | Area | What you will understand |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Traffic basics | merging, acceleration lanes, why cars stop at a lane end, time-to-collision (TTC) |
| 2 | The question | what "adaptive" means here; conditional advantages, not universal wins |
| 3 | The test bench | r2m3 in SUMO and its V&V record: "valid for intended use", never "proven" |
| 4 | The contestants | no control, tuned rules, and v3w (one PPO policy per CAV) |
| 5 | The referee | pre-registration, paired seeds, bootstrap CIs, confirmation versus replication |
| 6 | The E30 story | the edge, its replication, the 600-m reversal, the mechanism |
| 7 | The lessons | a result can pass every check and still rest on one simulator feature |
| 8 | Real data as a check | B0 asked whether simulated mergers stop more often than real ones; the NGSIM sites could not tell (V542) |
| 9 | Earlier lines | what was KILLed, withdrawn, closed or parked, and why |
| 10 | The engine room | ledger, frozen worktrees, rented machines, independent reviews |
| 11 | The thesis and papers | the approved wording and why a null result still makes a thesis |
